title: POC Scoping - Success Criteria Sign-off (Nimbus Analytics)
next_steps: Redwood to run benchmark on dedicated instance with customer sample traffic (SE)
Customer to share redacted sample dataset and core prompt set (Maya)
Redwood to share POC pricing and dedicated capacity options (AE)
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run and deep-dive week of 2025-04-21
action_items: Ethan Chen: configure benchmark harness and run initial throughput tests against 2 v100-equivalent instances by 2025-04-18
Maya Reed: provide 5k example prompts + expected outputs and redacted dataset by 2025-04-17
Samira Patel: send POC SOW and pricing tiers, include dedicated and hosted fallback options by 2025-04-16
Tom Alvarez: open networking access for Redwood test runners (IP allowlist) by 2025-04-18
summary: AE + SE align with customer on POC success criteria: p95 latency < 150ms for 512-token gen on dedicated pool, throughput 200 reqs/min sustained, accuracy/quality thresholds from evaluation set (>= 92% pass rate on rubric), and cost target < $X per 1M tokens. Acceptance tests and reporting format agreed: benchmark CSV + dashboard with token-level latency, cost estimate, and quality regressions.
header:
Date: 2025-04-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood Solutions Eng); Rajiv Kapoor (CTO, Nimbus), Maya Reed (ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Head of Infra), Ella Brooks (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to use this session to lock down the success criteria and acceptance tests for the POC. Uh Ethan will walk through the benchmark plan then we'll go into the pass/fail thresholds.
[00:22] Rajiv Kapoor: cool, thanks. Our timeline is pretty tight — we'd like a go/no-go in three weeks ideally. We can allocate infra and a tiny team.
[00:35] Ethan Chen: great. Quick note: we'll run two phases — a functional eval with the sample prompt set, then a production-like throughput run. For the throughput run we'll simulate the customers' 100k requests/day profile and peak burst of ~200 concurrent.
[00:50] Maya Reed: just to be clear, our current infra uses batching in-house and we do a lot of short chat style prompts, typical token length is 128-512 tokens. Latency is important for UX.
[01:05] Lina Gomez: when you say latency, is p50 or p95 the target?
[01:10] Maya Reed: p95. p50 is fine but p95 is what drives complaints.
[01:18] Ethan Chen: OK p95 it is. For dedicated we'll aim for p95 < 150ms on 512 token responses. On hosted we'd expect higher, but POC will be on a dedicated pool to validate economics.
[01:35] Tom Alvarez: 150ms p95 seems optimistic — what's the model baseline? Are we talking a smaller Llama derivative?
[01:44] Samira Patel: good question. For cost/speed tradeoff we'll test two model families: an optimized open LLM quantized profile (we'll call it rwd-opt-13b) and a lower-latency 7b variant. We'll include both in the benchmark so you can see quality vs cost.
[02:05] Rajiv Kapoor: and quality thresholds — how do we define pass/fail?
[02:10] Ethan Chen: we usually use a rubric on the eval set — for classification or extraction we use exact-match or F1, for generative we use a human-rated pass rate. For this POC: target >= 92% pass rate on the curated prompt set (rated by your SMEs), and hallucination rate < 3% measured by a set of hallucination checks.
[02:30] Maya Reed: we can do the SME ratings. We'll be conservative but want to be realistic.
[02:38] Ella Brooks: on reporting — what format will Redwood provide?
[02:42] Samira Patel: benchmark CSV with per-request latency, token counts, model variant, cost estimate columns, plus a dashboard export (Grafana/Prometheus style) and an executive summary PDF. We'll also include the prompt-level failure causes.
[03:00] Tom Alvarez: networking and security — we need SSO and audit logs. Also, data shouldn't leave our VPC unless it's hashed.
[03:10] Ethan Chen: for POC we can use a private test VPC peering or a temporary allowlist. We'll also enable key rotation and KMS integration for any payloads. For production Private option we support VPC and on-prem packages.
[03:28] Rajiv Kapoor: does Redwood have SOC 2? We need the security pack.
[03:32] Samira Patel: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO posture — I'll attach the security pack and compliance docs after the call.
[03:40] Maya Reed: one more on measurement: we want token-level cost and per-route breakdown because some prompts are 5x more expensive.
[03:51] Ethan Chen: absolutely, Redwood Console gives token-level cost and per-route dashboards. We'll include the cost delta between quantized 13b and 7b.
[04:05] Samira Patel: ok let's write down the POC success criteria for signoff: 1) Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token gen on dedicated pool; 2) Throughput: sustain 200 reqs/min with <= 10% tail latency increase; 3) Quality: >= 92% pass rate on curated prompts, hallucination < 3%; 4) Cost: model/config cost per 1M tokens below your internal threshold — we can estimate and iterate; 5) Security: test run must be performed inside allowed network with audit logging enabled.
[04:40] Rajiv Kapoor: sounds good. On the cost target, can you give a ballpark so we can decide?
[04:46] Samira Patel: yes we'll provide an initial estimate after we have your sample token distribution. We'll show cost per 1M tokens for each model variant and quantization level.
[04:55] Maya Reed: acceptance test specifics? I want a clear go/no-go criteria for the sign-off meeting at the end of the POC.
[05:02] Ethan Chen: go/no-go will be: all hard thresholds met (latency, throughput, security); and no more than one major quality regression compared to baseline. We'll deliver a report with pass/fail per test and an aggregated verdict.
[05:18] Ella Brooks: baseline meaning current internal model?
[05:21] Maya Reed: yes we'll provide a small baseline set.
[05:24] Ethan Chen: perfect. We'll run A/B comparisons and produce confusion matrices / per-prompt failure reasons.
[05:35] [00:05:40] Rajiv Kapoor: how long does the benchmark run take?
[05:40] Ethan Chen: functional eval is a couple hours, throughput run we recommend a 2-4 hour sustained window to see steady-state; plus a 30 minute soak. So total ≈ 4 hours including setup.
[05:52] Tom Alvarez: for the dedicated pool, what instance types are you using? We need to size our network.
[05:58] Lina Gomez: we'll propose instance profiles in the runbook — typically a 4-GPU cluster depending on model. For rwd-opt-13b we recommend A100-80GB equivalents for headroom; for 7b a 2-GPU config could be enough.
[06:15] Tom Alvarez: ok we'll aim to provision similar.
[06:20] Rajiv Kapoor: what about caching? We have a lot of prefix repetition in our prompts.
[06:25] Ethan Chen: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and automatic continuous batching. For POC we'll enable caching and run a second pass with cache disabled to show delta.
[06:35] Maya Reed: good — we want to see both.
[06:40] Samira Patel: acceptance report format: 1) executive summary, 2) CSV with per-request metrics, 3) dashboards link, 4) quality rubric results plus SME notes. Agreed?
[06:52] Maya Reed: yes.
[06:55] Rajiv Kapoor: any regulatory constraints? Data residency?
[07:00] Ella Brooks: all data must stay in US and EU regions for now.
[07:04] Ethan Chen: POC will run in your chosen region; we can pin region and avoid cross-region calls.
[07:12] Samira Patel: action items recap — I'll send SOW and security pack; Ethan will run the harness; Maya will send sample prompts; Tom will open networking. We'll aim to run benchmarks week of 2025-04-21.
[07:30] Rajiv Kapoor: ok timeline works. One question on reporting cadence for regressions — can we get daily reports during the POC?
[07:38] Ethan Chen: yes we can push daily summary emails and a live dashboard with token-level breakdowns.
[07:44] Maya Reed: on hallucination measurement — what tooling are you using?
[07:48] Ethan Chen: a mix of automated heuristics plus SME checks. We'll flag potential hallucinations then have your SMEs validate a random sample.
[07:58] Samira Patel: any other concerns?
[08:00] Tom Alvarez: just the usual — ensure RBAC and audit logs are on, and that logs won't be forwarded to any third-party telemetry.
[08:08] Lina Gomez: noted, we'll disable telemetry and ensure logs are retained per your policy.
[08:14] Rajiv Kapoor: finale — can you put the go/no-go thresholds in a single table in the SOW? Makes sign-off simpler.
[08:20] Samira Patel: yes we'll include a single acceptance criteria table with pass/fail analytics.
[08:27] Ella Brooks: if we pass, what's the next step for Dedicated?
[08:31] Samira Patel: from there we discuss reserved capacity terms and tuning for production; AE will lead commercial discussions.
[08:38] Rajiv Kapoor: perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:41] Samira Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
[08:45] [End of call]
